Attempt first

Two equal masses m lie on a smooth horizontal surface and are joined by a light string of total length 2a. The midpoint of the initially taut string is pulled vertically upward by a small constant force F. When the masses are separated by 2x, determine the magnitude of the acceleration of either mass.

Conditions

  • Horizontal surface is frictionless.
  • String is light and remains taut.
  • Each half-string has length a.

Common wrong route

Taking T=F/2 without resolving the angled string segments.

    Attempt first

    A block moving on a rough horizontal surface stops after losing its kinetic energy to friction. The same surface is then inclined at 30 degrees and the block is projected up the incline with the same initial speed. Judge these claims: (1) the energy dissipated by friction before stopping is smaller on the incline; (2) the coefficient of friction becomes smaller when the plane is inclined.

    Conditions

    • Same pair of surfaces is used.
    • Initial speed is the same in both trials.
    • Incline angle is 30 degrees.

    Common wrong route

    Assuming a smaller friction force means the coefficient itself has changed.

            Attempt first

            Two touching blocks m1=1 kg and m2=2 kg rest on an incline of angle theta, with m1 placed just above m2 (up the slope), so m1 presses on m2. The plane is smooth under m1; for m2, static and kinetic friction coefficients are both 0.3. Determine which friction expression applies to m2 at theta = 5°, 10°, 15° and 20°. Candidate expressions are: (1) m2 g sin⁡theta\sin theta; (2) (m1+m2)g sin⁡theta\sin theta; (3) 0.3 m2 g cos⁡theta\cos theta; (4) 0.3(m1+m2)g cos⁡theta\cos theta.

            Conditions

            • m1=1 kg; m2=2 kg.
            • Only m2 has friction with the plane, mu=0.3.
            • Use tan⁡5.5∘\tan 5.5^{\circ}≈0.1, tan⁡11.5∘\tan 11.5^{\circ}≈0.2, tan⁡16.5∘\tan 16.5^{\circ}≈0.3.
            • m1 is directly up-slope of m2 and pushes on it; m2 is the lower block.

            Common wrong route

            Using m2 g sin⁡theta\sin theta as the required static friction and ignoring the contact force transmitted by m1.
